sentences.text: [serious] Forty, and earning eight thousand a month? Fidelity says you should have two hundred and eighty-eight thousand saved.
Thirty: ninety-six thousand. Fifty: five seventy-six. Sixty: seven sixty-eight. Sixty-seven: nine hundred and sixty thousand. Where are you?

visual.title: Where are you? $8K/mo pay
visual.source: Fidelity guideline: 1x salary by 30, 3x by 40, 6x by 50, 8x by 60, 10x by 67

sentences.text: [reassuring] Behind? Most advice says spend less. But that won't work unless the saving happens first.
Fidelity assumes fifteen percent of your pay, every year, from age twenty-five. Your four-oh-one-k and any match count toward it.

visual.source: Your 401(k) and any employer match count. A guideline, not a rule.

sentences.text: Starting at forty? Fifteen percent of eight thousand is twelve hundred a month. By sixty-seven, that's three hundred and eighty-eight thousand, before any growth.

visual.source: 15% of $8,000 a month, for 27 years. No investment growth assumed.

sentences.text: So it leaves on payday, before anything else. The rest gets one daily number that adjusts when you overspend.
[warm] So, where are you? Find your age, then make payday the day you save. Save first. Then spend what's safe. Try it at Divvyup dot com.
